themes_detail.label: Non-Emergency Police Calls Spike
themes_detail.summary: Non-emergency police matters complaints surged to 18 this week versus a baseline average of 3.0 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 500% spike with z-score of 13.42—signaling either a sudden public safety concern or emerging quality-of-life issue in Bed-Stuy this week.
evidence: 18 non-emergency police complaints filed this week vs. 3.0 per week average over prior 8 weeks
z-score of 13.42 indicates statistically extreme outlier

Concurrent spike in 'Obstruction' complaints (13 this week vs 3.6 avg, +259%) and 'Dumpster Complaint' complaints (4 this week vs 0.8 avg, +433%) suggest environmental factors may be triggering police calls
reporting_angles: Investigate what specific non-emergency police matters drove this week's spike—e.g., trespassing, loitering, disorderly conduct—by interviewing NYPD and residents
Map the geographic distribution of these 18 calls to identify if spike is localized to specific blocks or dispersed across CD303

themes_detail.label: Lot Condition Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Lot condition complaints exploded to 7 this week versus a baseline of 0.2 per week over 8 weeks—a 2,700% increase with z-score 10.21—indicating potential emergence of neglected vacant properties or illegal dumping in Bed-Stuy.
evidence: 7 lot condition complaints filed this week vs. 0.2 per week baseline over prior 8 weeks
z-score of 10.21 is second-most extreme statistical anomaly in dataset
Correlates with spike in 'Dumpster Complaint' (+433% this week) and 'Obstruction' (+259% this week), suggesting systemic debris/waste management problem
reporting_angles: Identify which specific lots are generating complaints; cross-reference with NYC Department of Finance and DOB data to determine ownership and vacancy status
Interview community residents and local businesses about whether illegal dumping or property neglect is visible in the neighborhood

themes_detail.label: Street Infrastructure Damage Spike
themes_detail.summary: Street sign complaints—both missing (3 reported 3 weeks ago, +1,100% vs 0.2 avg, z-score 6.35) and damaged (3 reported last week, +380% vs 0.6 avg, z-score 4.91)—signal coordinated street infrastructure degradation or vandalism in Bed-Stuy over the past 3 weeks.
evidence: 3 missing street sign complaints 3 weeks ago vs 0.2 baseline (z-score 6.35, +1,100%)
3 damaged street sign complaints last week vs 0.6 baseline (z-score 4.91, +380%)
Combined signal suggests sustained infrastructure problem over 3-4 week window
reporting_angles: Request NYC Department of Transportation data on street sign maintenance and replacement schedules for CD303; determine if there's a maintenance backlog or vandalism pattern
Photograph damaged/missing signs and map their location to identify if damage is concentrated in specific corridors

themes_detail.label: Abandoned Bikes Accumulation
themes_detail.summary: Abandoned bike complaints jumped to 6 reported 3 weeks ago versus a baseline of 0.8 per week—a 700% spike with z-score 6.33—indicating either a bike-share service issue or illegal dumping of discarded bicycles in Bed-Stuy.
evidence: 6 abandoned bike complaints filed 3 weeks ago vs 0.8 per week baseline over prior 8 weeks (z-score 6.33, +700%)
No follow-up spike data for past 2 weeks; unclear if problem is ongoing or resolved
reporting_angles: Contact Citi Bike and other bike-share operators to determine if there's a fleet management issue or if abandoned bikes are private property
Determine whether complaints cluster geographically near transit hubs or public spaces

themes_detail.label: Smoking/Vaping Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Smoking or vaping complaints spiked to 11 complaints 2 weeks ago versus a baseline of 3.5 per week—a 214% increase with z-score 4.33—possibly reflecting enforcement of indoor smoking regulations or residential frustration with outdoor vaping in shared spaces.
evidence: 11 smoking/vaping complaints filed 2 weeks ago vs 3.5 per week baseline over prior 8 weeks (z-score 4.33, +214%)
No sustained follow-up spike in most recent week; unclear if trend is ongoing
reporting_angles: Identify whether complaints are concentrated in residential buildings, parks, or transit areas to pinpoint the problem zone
Check if NYC Department of Health enforcement actions or public education campaigns in Bed-Stuy preceded the spike
